mannar-thambapavani-wind-adb.conditions_add: ADB's loan paper for the Mannar wind farm sets out what the Ceylon Electricity Board was to do. The resettlement plan "will be updated" once the final turbine designs fixed the impacts, and CEB was to "submit monitoring reports to ADB semiannually". The environmental management plan "will be incorporated into civil works contracts", a biodiversity management plan was to "ensure no net loss of biodiversity at the wind power generation site", and "curtailment of wind turbines during the bird migratory period" is listed as a mitigation measure. CEB was also to set up a project management unit and "provide environmental monitoring reports to ADB quarterly during construction". The paper says the detailed covenants are in the draft loan and guarantee agreements, which it does not reproduce (Asian Development Bank, Report and Recommendation of the President, 2017).

why.safeguard: a biodiversity management plan was to "ensure no net loss of biodiversity at the wind power generation site"
why.admin: CEB was also to set up a project management unit

east-west-highway-khevi.conditions_add: For the Shorapani-Argveta section, ADB's loan paper says a resettlement plan prepared for JICA was "under implementation and more than 85% completed", and that "A corrective action plan prepared to cover gaps between JICA and ADB's Safeguard Policy Statement" was in place for this project. The construction supervision consultant's resettlement and environmental specialists were to "prepare semiannual safeguards monitoring reports for ADB's review and disclosure". The ministry, the Roads Department and the ETCIC "will maintain adequate and separate project records and accounts, which an independent auditor will audit annually", and "Procurement of all contracts will follow the ADB Procurement Policy". The government and the Roads Department gave an assurance that implementation "shall conform to all applicable ADB requirements"; the paper says the covenants themselves are set out in the draft loan agreement, which it does not reproduce (Asian Development Bank, Report and Recommendation of the President, 2020).

kashang-hydro-lippa-adb.conditions_add: ADB's $800 million facility paid out in tranches, and its loan paper lists criteria a subproject had to meet to be selected and approved for financing. Among them were "a land acquisition and resettlement plan that meets the requirements of ADB's Involuntary Resettlement Policy (2005)", "an indigenous peoples development plan (IPDP) that meets the requirements of ADB's Policy on Indigenous Peoples (1998)", and "an environmental management and monitoring plan that meets the requirements of ADB's Environment Policy (2002)", each submitted to ADB for review; summary environmental assessments had to be "made available to the public 120 days before a periodic financing request (PFR) is submitted to ADB". The state power company "shall maintain separate accounts for each subproject and for its overall operations", the state "will onlend funds to HPPCL under arm's-length terms to ensure commercial discipline", and civil works were to be bought by international competitive bidding. The first tranche covered "the civil works for the 65 MW Kashang I Hydroelectric Project" (Asian Development Bank, Report and Recommendation of the President, 2008).

noor-ouarzazate-pasture.conditions_add: These terms come from the World Bank's 2014 appraisal of the Noor II and Noor III plants, four years after Morocco's solar agency MASEN bought the land in 2010. The appraisal says the two plant sites "have already been acquired by MASEN" and gives no acquisition date, so its terms did not govern that purchase. Before related civil works MASEN had to give the Bank land acquisition plans for review and complete the resettlement measures in them, "including the full payment of compensation", and could not authorise civil works "before the relevant SESIA is prepared, adopted and disclosed". It had to prepare an environmental and social management report "on a bi-annual basis" during building. The loan agreements require, "as a condition to disbursement under the agreements, that the SPVs establish an accounting and financial management system" acceptable to the Bank, and the borrower's "Equity shall remain positive on a yearly basis" from fiscal year 2015 (World Bank, Project Appraisal Document, 2014).

upper-kotmale-jbic.conditions_add: JICA's own review of the project gives the loan terms. For both phases the "Conditions for procurement" are listed as "Tied": Phase I as "Tied (Special Yen Loan)" and Phase II as "Tied (Special Terms of Economic Partnership (STEP))". The review does not name the eligible countries, but says that "by applying rules for country of origin of goods and services, the bidders are restricted", which the executing agency said cut competition, and every main contractor and the main consultant it lists is a Japanese company. Phase I carried 0.95% interest on the main part and Phase II 0.20%, each repayable over 40 years with a 10-year grace period (JICA, ex-post evaluation, 2016).

mahenge-graphite-ulanga-faru.conditions_add: These terms were set after the move. Black Rock's filing on the US$179 million facilities from DBSA, IDC and CRDB, signed on 13 September 2024, is about five years after the 2019-2020 relocation, so the lenders' conditions did not apply to it. Before the first drawdown the company must put in "the required project equity prior to first drawdown" and carry out "implementation of technical, environmental and social actions", and the agreement is "subject to satisfaction of customary conditions precedent and approval by the Bank of Tanzania". From first production the borrower must hold equity support "equal to the next 12 months of debt service", which "increases to 24 months debt service" without enough offtake, and must have "sufficient offtake agreements in place to provide 1x debt service cover". Each facility is limited to set uses: the term loan to "Mahenge construction costs and other eligible costs", the bank guarantee facility to "Mine closure and rehabilitation obligations" (Black Rock Mining, ASX announcement, 2024).

why.fincov: must have "sufficient offtake agreements in place to provide 1x debt service cover"

tendaho-sugar-india-exim-afar.conditions_add: The credit was tied to Indian suppliers. Global Trade Review reports a "US$640mn credit commitment from the Export-Import Bank of India (India Exim)" for Ethiopia's sugar industry, which must cover "at least 75% of contract values for goods and services that are imported from India", and says India Exim "loaned US$350mn in 2009 for Indian firm OIA to build a sugar factory in Tendaho, northern Ethiopia". A Global Trade Alert record of a 2011 Exim credit to Ethiopia for sugar says it "requires that at least 75% of the contract price for goods and services associated with the project is sourced" from India; the rest of that record's description sits behind a sign-in (Global Trade Review; Global Trade Alert).

The office also found that "IFC did not include in the ESAP sufficient requirements" on deadlines, expertise, documentation and reporting for the company's public consultation and disclosure plan (Compliance Advisor Ombudsman, compliance monitoring report, 2018).

A 2009 renovation paid for by the UN drug office, costing $95,200, was meant "to meet basic standards of hygiene and comfort and to separate young residents from adults", and the UN office said "UNODC does not support the construction of new centers in Lao PDR". The report says "No organization identified a specific mechanism to monitor the human rights of detainees in Somsanga", and does not describe any donor attaching conditions to its money (Human Rights Watch, 2011).

haiti-creole-pig-eradication.conditions_add: The eradication agreement signed by Haiti's government and the Interamerican Institute for Cooperation in Agriculture said owners of hogs slaughtered in the 1978 campaign were to be compensated "prior to the depopulation stage of the Project"; Multinational Monitor says "No compensation was given to the peasants whose pigs near the Dominican border were exterminated in 1978". To get a replacement pig a farmer had to be "unable to buy the pig", agree to "learn how to take care of the pig", have a pen made with "appropriate materials", guarantee that pigs could not reach human waste, and return "one pig from the second generation litter to the distribution center". The contract forbade feeding animals "wastes or other ingredients which are not part of the formula approved by the project" (Multinational Monitor, 1985).
